turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. You asked for this meeting, so I assume you have an explanation for why my son found a zero on his phone in the middle of class.
Totally unrelated, but you're good with words.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen asked anything before it went in?
I have to email a parent tonight about a fight in the cafeteria. Could you help me word it?

I'm not here to draft your emails, Hale. Put it together yourself, after we've dealt with Owen.

Who decided on the zero?
Just a couple of sentences. You'd nail it.
Save it, Hale. I have eighteen minutes, and they're for Owen. Your own procedure, 4.2, says a parent is called before any mark goes in, and nobody called me.
